thought_title: One choir in tune with the bishop

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Ὅθεν πρέπει ὑμῖν συντρέχειν τῇ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου γνώμῃ, ὅπερ καὶ ποιεῖτε. τὸ γὰρ ἀξιονόμαστον ὑμῶν πρεσβυτέριον, τοῦ θεοῦ ἄξιον, οὕτως συνήρμοσται τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ, ὡς χορδαὶ κιθάρᾳ. διὰ τοῦτο ἐν τῇ ὁμονοίᾳ ὑμῶν καὶ συμφώνῳ ἀγάπῃ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ᾅδεται. [2] καὶ οἱ κατ’ ἄνδρα δὲ χορὸς γίνεσθε, ἵνα σύμφωνοι ὄντες ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ, χρῶμα θεοῦ λαβόντες ἐν ἑνότητι, ᾅδητε ἐν φωνῇ μιᾷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῷ πατρί, ἵνα ὑμῶν καὶ ἀκούσῃ καὶ ἐπιγινώσκῃ, δἰ ὦν εὖ πράσσετε, μέλη ὄντας τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ. χρήσιμον οὖν ἐστὶν ὑμᾶς ἐν ἀμώμῳ ἑνότητι εἶναι, ἵνα καὶ θεοῦ πάντοτε μετέχητε.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore it is fitting for you to run in agreement with the mind of the bishop, which you are in fact doing. For your presbytery, rightly famous and worthy of God, is fitted to the bishop as strings are to a lyre. That is why Jesus Christ is sung in your concord and harmonious love. And each of you, man by man, become a choir, so that being in tune in concord, taking up God's key in unity, you may sing with one voice through Jesus Christ to the Father, so that he may both hear you and recognize, by the good things you do, that you are members of his Son. It is useful, then, for you to be in blameless unity, so that you may also always have a share in God.

lemmas.gloss: color; in music, a key or mode

pass_b_english: So it is right for you to keep pace with the bishop's mind, and you already do. Your presbytery, deservedly renowned and worthy of God, is tuned to the bishop like strings to a lyre. That is why Jesus Christ is sung in your concord and in your harmonious love.

Now each of you, one by one, become a choir. Be in tune with one another in concord. Take your pitch from God, all together, and sing with one voice through Jesus Christ to the Father. Then he will hear you, and from your good works he will know you as members of his Son. It does you good, then, to live in blameless unity, so that you may always share in God.

choices.why: χρῶμα in music is the key or coloring of a scale; the singers take God's key.
rejected: taking up the song of God (ANF; loose)

choices.why: κιθάρα is a lyre, not a modern harp; the image is tuning.

choices.english: each of you, one by one, become a choir
choices.why: Keeps Ignatius's paradox: individuals, one by one, together make a single choir.
μετέχω is to have a share in; Ignatius speaks of participation in God.
rejected: enjoy communion with God (ANF; adds a term)

anf_compare.notes: Sense aligned. ANF 'being harmonious in love' should be 'in concord' (ὁμονοίᾳ); 'song of God' loosens χρῶμα θεοῦ (God's key).

notes: Whole chapter 4 (sections 1-2) matches the ANF span.
Possible echoes kept out of the reading text: Romans 15:6 (with one mouth glorify God and Father); 1 Corinthians 12:27 (members of Christ). Neither is close enough in wording to cite inline.

review.notes: Paragraph 1 checked in full against both passes. Source is the named Ephesians 4 choir passage (συντρέχειν τῇ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου γνώμῃ through θεοῦ πάντοτε μετέχητε). Pass A keeps every clause: fitting concurrence with the bishop’s γνώμη (ὅπερ καὶ ποιεῖτε), the ἀξιονόμαστον presbytery fitted ὡς χορδαὶ κιθάρᾳ, Christ sung (ᾅδεται) in concord, the one choir, purpose-subjunctives, blameless unity, and participation. No negation is reversed; agency (you concur/sing; the Father hears; Christ is sung) and doctrine (members of his Son; share in God) hold. No inline citation is present to mismatch; notes correctly withhold loose echoes. Title names the thought. Fail is Pass B’s mood: ‘ἵνα σύμφωνοι ὄντες ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ, χρῶμα θεοῦ λαβόντες ἐν ἑνότητι, ᾅδητε ἐν φωνῇ μιᾷ’ becomes commands, and ‘ἵνα ὑμῶν καὶ ἀκούσῃ καὶ ἐπιγινώσκῃ’ becomes ‘Then he will hear you’. Dropped γάρ and καί are minor and not the fail.
reasons: Pass B turns purpose and circumstance into extra commands. Greek ‘ἵνα σύμφωνοι ὄντες ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ, χρῶμα θεοῦ λαβόντες ἐν ἑνότητι, ᾅδητε ἐν φωνῇ μιᾷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῷ πατρί’ is one ἵνα-subjunctive (may sing) with participles; Pass A keeps ‘so that being in tune in concord, taking up God's key in unity, you may sing with one voice through Jesus Christ to the Father’. Pass B has ‘Be in tune with one another in concord. Take your pitch from God, all together, and sing with one voice through Jesus Christ to the Father.’ Pitch for χρῶμα is allowed; the imperative rewrite is not.

Pass B replaces purpose-possibility with a predicted result. Greek ‘ἵνα ὑμῶν καὶ ἀκούσῃ καὶ ἐπιγινώσκῃ, δἰ ὦν εὖ πράσσετε, μέλη ὄντας τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ’ is so that he may hear and recognize. Pass A: ‘so that he may both hear you and recognize, by the good things you do, that you are members of his Son.’ Pass B: ‘Then he will hear you, and from your good works he will know you as members of his Son.’ ‘Then’ plus ‘will’ is not the subjunctive aim.
